newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian parties set final meeting over budget row.
newsitem.headline: Italian parties set final meeting over budget row.

text.p: Coalition parliamentary party leaders will meet their counterparts from the opposition Freedom Alliance at 1400 GMT in a final bid to resolve the stand-off over the 1997 budget, political sources said.

Silvio Berlusconi's centre-right Freedom Alliance said on Monday it would not vote on the budget package, to protest at a government request to set policy in several key areas without recourse to parliament.
Seeking to end the opposition revolt, Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco earlier today gave more details of the planned revision of income tax -- one of the most disputed areas of the budget package.
The Freedom Alliance made no official comment on Visco's speech, however Rocco Buttiglione, leader of the centrist CDU party and a Berlusconi ally, said it was "confused and insufficient".
Fabio Mussi, parliamentary party leader of the largest coalition party, the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), said the government had already conceded a lot of ground to the opposition.
"The (1400 GMT) meeting is the final chance, after which we guarantee to the country that the budget will be passed according to the timetable," he told reporters.
The budget is due to be approved by the lower house on November 14 after which it passes to the Senate (upper house) for ratification.
Debate on the package, which was suspended in the lower house earlier on Tuesday, will resume at 1530 GMT. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
